BiblicalUsage: An answer — the noun, four times. The priests demand one of John in John 1:22, that they may give an answer to them that sent them; Pilate asks Jesus whence He is in John 19:9, but Jesus gave him no answer. The boy Jesus in the temple astonishes all who hear Him with His understanding and answers in Luke 2:47, and the spies in Luke 20:26 marvel at His answer and hold their peace.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the answers in these four verses trace the whole range: an answer demanded, an answer refused, an answer that astonishes, and an answer that silences. Jesus gives the answer His hearers need — or withholds the one they have no right to — and either way the questioners are left with nothing more to say.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; John the Baptist; Pontius Pilate
